VitaFoods Inc. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the VitaFoods Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the presentation portion of the call. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss VitaFoods Inc.'s Q3 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Maria Gonzalez, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Growth Officer; and Lisa Chen, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Maria.

Maria Gonzalez (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on seven key areas: key achievements and challenges in the quarter; volume and price/mix analysis; discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies; e-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue; impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue; market share trends for major brands; and capital expenditure plans and priorities.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah to provide more detail on our financial results and walk through these key areas.

Sarah Jenkins (CFO):
Thank you, Maria. As Maria mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2024. Net sales were $2.85 billion, representing a 7.2% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 38.2%, impacted by elevated commodity costs in dairy, edible oils, and sugar, partially offset by pricing actions and mix improvements. Operating income was $320 million, and adjusted earnings per share were $1.12. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.4 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Let me now dive deeper into the seven key areas Maria highlighted, starting with the key achievements and challenges that shaped our Q3 results as we navigate a dynamic Food & Beverage landscape. Overall, adjusted EBITDA came in at $425 million, up 9% year-over-year, with margins expanding 50 basis points to 14.9%, reflecting disciplined cost management and favorable mix benefits.

On achievements, volume growth stood out at 4.1% globally, outpacing the industry average of 2.3% according to Nielsen data. This was driven by our HealthForward portfolio, now 28% of total sales, up from 22% a year ago. Premium plant-based snacks and functional beverages, such as our OatFlex protein bars and VitaQuench electrolyte drinks, delivered 22% volume growth, gaining share in the $15 billion U.S. better-for-you segment. We expanded market share by 1.2 points to 11.4% in IRI-tracked channels, ahead of competitors like Kellogg's RXBAR and PepsiCo's Gatorade Zero.

In North America, we posted 9.5% organic revenue growth to $1.6 billion, powered by e-commerce now at 18% of U.S. sales versus 12% last year, supported by Amazon Fresh and Instacart partnerships. The away-from-home channel surged with foodservice volumes up 12%, as quick-service restaurants including Starbucks and McDonald's increased private-label orders for our savory dips and ready-to-heat meals.

In APAC, Greater China achieved 15% growth via localized mango-lassi yogurt drinks tapping the $8 billion fermented dairy trend, gaining 2.5 share points against Danone's Activia. Latin America added 11% growth, highlighted by Brazil's affordable hydration pouches amid drought challenges.

Operationally, our SAP S/4HANA ERP rollout across 15 plants cut inventory costs by 8%, freeing $22 million in working capital. An AI-driven demand sensing pilot with IBM Watson boosted forecast accuracy by 14% and reduced stockouts by 22% for high-velocity items like our chip lines, vital amid volatile cocoa and palm oil prices.

On sustainability, we reduced Scope 3 emissions 25% through regenerative agriculture with 200 cocoa farmers in Côte d'Ivoire, supporting our 2030 net-zero goal and earning a Dow Jones Sustainability Index listing for F&B.

Challenges included stubborn commodity inflation—dairy up 12%, edible oils 18%, sugar 9%—adding $85 million to COGS despite 70% hedges, pressuring gross margins 120 basis points pre-mitigation, similar to Mondelez's cocoa issues. FX dragged $45 million, mainly from 15% depreciation in the Brazilian real and Turkish lira, hitting emerging margins. EMEA revenues were flat at $450 million due to Western Europe downtrading to private labels amid 7% food-at-home inflation per Kantar, while EU PFAS packaging rules delayed launches costing $12 million. Supply chain issues from Red Sea reroutings raised ocean freight 25%, and private-label aggression from Aldi and Lidl eroded 0.8 share points in salty snacks.

Strategically, we're divesting two legacy beverage brands for $150 million to fund high-growth RTD coffee M&A, investing $200 million in precision fermentation for dairy alternatives targeting a $50 billion TAM by 2028 per McKinsey. With indulgence-with-health trends like low-sugar chocolates, we're launching 40 new SKUs in Q4. This resilience lets us raise full-year guidance to 6-7% organic growth and 15%+ EBITDA margins.

Next, volume and price/mix analysis, which breaks down our top-line performance for transparency into revenue growth management—or RGM—strategies. Organic growth was 5.8%, comprising 4.1% volume and 1.7% price/mix tailwind, marking three straight quarters of positive volumes after -2% in Q4 2022 peak inflation.

By segment: Beverages (45% of sales, $1.28 billion, +6% organic) saw 1% volume from zero-sugar innovations like VitalQuench Hydrate gaining 250 bps ACV to 85% in North America, offsetting 2% legacy CSD decline mirroring Coca-Cola and PepsiCo. Price/mix +5% from 6-8% increases on premium RTD teas and functionals, plus 200 bps mix shift; RGM tech cut trade spend 50 bps to 18%.

Snacks & Confectionery ($855 million, +9% organic): 4% volume led by 6% savory snacks from ProteinCrunch bar relaunch with 15g plant protein, +1.5 share points vs. Frito-Lay; price/mix +5% from 7% elastic hikes and 150 bps premium flavor mix like Sriracha Lime Kettle Chips.

Nutritionals ($675 million, +8% organic): 2% volumes with +12% plant-based dairy like OatVital milk via e-commerce; price/mix +6% from 5% yogurt hikes and 300 bps premium Greek/probiotic shift.

Regionally: North America (55%, +7% organic) volumes +3% on eight launches to 92% household penetration, price/mix +4%; Europe (20%, +5%) flat volumes on HFSS curbs but +6% price/mix; Latin America & EM (25%, +15%) volumes +8% on nutrition packs, price/mix +7%.

Our Premiumize, Digitize, Localize RGM framework, post-$200 million legacy divestitures and Revenue Growth Management Center with Black Book/IRI ML, drives 2x trade ROI. Q4 outlook: 5-7% organic, volumes +4% on 12 health launches, pricing +3-4%, mix +2 points.

Turning to pricing actions and RGM strategies, pivotal for our 5.8% organic growth outpacing NielsenIQ's 3.8% industry average—third straight mid-single-digit quarter. Decomposition: 4.1% pricing, -0.8% volume offset by 2.5% mix. Targeted 3.8% list increases yielded 4.5% net realization post-trade normalization, elasticity -1.8 vs. historical -2.2.

Mix +2.9% from premiumization: VitalHydrate functionals +18% volume, CrunchElite proteins +22%, diluting CSDs -5%. Beverages (55% of $2.85B) shifted 3.2 points to low/no-sugar (42% segment share). Snacks saw baked/nut growth +15%.

North America (62%, $1.77B): pricing +5.2% via 4-6% hikes on 70% portfolio, mix +3.8% e-comm premium like ZenTea kombucha +25%, trade efficiency to 28%. EMEA (22%, $627M): pricing +2.9% less-for-less on premiums, mix +4.1% plant-based +28%. APAC/LatAm: pricing 6.1%/7.2%, mix +2.5% occasion packs.

Tech backbone: AI pricing platform with PROS, IRI/Nielsen data for 92% elasticity accuracy, cut ineffective spend 14% ($220M annualized save); e.g., 4% nacho hikes at -2.3 elasticity. Portfolio health scoring rationalized 12% low SKUs. Eco-packaging justified 2-3% premiums (68% millennial WTP).

North Star: profitable share growth in polarized landscape—value tiers for Walmart/Kroger, premium for Costco/7-Eleven. FY2025 guide: 4-6% organic, pricing 3.5-4.5%, mix 2-3%, volumes +1.5 ACV. This drove 110 bps margin expansion to 32.4% gross.

On e-commerce sales growth and revenue contribution, a standout at $430 million, +45% YoY and 15% QoQ, now 15% of total revenues—double Q3 2023's 7% and up from Q2's 12%, with 50%+ CAGR since FY2021 outpacing U.S. e-grocery's 13% per IRI.

Driven by perishables strategy for meal kits, NutriOat plant beverages, protein snacks; 68% shoppers prioritize quick delivery per NPS. AOV +18% to $85 via bundling high-margin combos.

U.S. (72%, $310M, +52%): DTC +65% on Shopify AI personalization (conversion 3.2% to 4.8%); Amazon Fresh/Whole Foods 28%, Instacart/DoorDash 15% for perishables. Europe ($55M equiv., +35%, 18% regional): Tesco/Carrefour ties, localized SKUs/subscriptions at 25% repeat. APAC ($43M, +30%) via Shopee/Lazada.

Invested $25M YTD in 45 dark stores with Ocado automation, SAP IBP for 40% fewer stockouts; e-comm margins +250 bps to 42% DTC. Data from 2.5M users spots trends like +30% functional bev post-Ozempic for GLP-1 NutriShakes. Mitigating 10% last-mile freight, regulatory via contracts/opt-ins.

Q4 guide: $500-520M, full-year 16-17%; target 25% by FY2027 with intl DTC/Web3.

Regarding impact of foreign exchange rates, with 45% revenues international on $11.4B TTM, USD strength was a $45 million headwind. Reported +7.2% to $2.85B; constant currency +8.3% on 4.1% volumes, 4.2% pricing. Cumulative YTD $128M drag from USD +8.2% trade-weighted.

Europe (22%): euro -6.7%, $18M hit; reported -1.2% vs. +4.5% CC on NutriCrunch +5% volumes post-sugar tax. APAC (15%): yuan/AUD/JPY weakness $14M; reported -3.4% vs. +2.8% CC on sparkling +6%. LatAm (8%): $2M tailwind from real, reported +7.6% vs. +6.9% CC on snacks.

Mitigation: 75% 2024 revenue hedged 2.5% favorable; local ASEAN production -30% import reliance; 4-6% pricing pass-through. Diversifying via coffee roasting Colombia/Brazil, AI FX forecasting to cap <100 bps drag. Q4: neutral to 100 bps headwind.

Market share trends from IRI/Nielsen show +110 bps YoY to 14.2% aggregate—third quarter acceleration. Beverages (45% revenues): AquaPure sparkling +2.3 pts to 22.1% value (vs. Aquafina -1.1 pts), Zest Cola flat volume +0.9 pts; VitaBoost functionals +2.1 pts to 8.2%.

Snacks +4.2% category: CrunchMax +1.8 pts to 15.4% vs. Frito-Lay -0.4 pts; NutriBar +70 bps to 11.9%. Dairy: YoGlow +1.5 pts to 13.7% vs. Activia 11.4%.

North America +210 bps to 18.5% on e-comm/velocity; Europe flat 12.1%; APAC +3.2 pts to 9.8% (ZenLeaf 14%); LatAm +40 bps to 11.2%.

Brand Acceleration Engine ($250M invest): innovation (12 SKUs, AI flavors -30% TTM), route-to-market (92% ACV, D2C +22% wallet), sustainability (85% recyclable +1.2 pts). Q4 +80-100 bps on campaigns; M&A firepower ahead.

Finally, capital expenditure plans for FY2025 at $850 million, 4.2% of sales, +12% YoY—blended payback <3 years, ROIC >15% by FY2027. Priorities amid health shifts, inflation, supply resilience.

Manufacturing (45%, $382M): $150M Monterrey greenfield for RTD coffee/energy (Krones aseptic -18% cost/case); $120M Chicago cobots (+25% throughput); $80M Rotterdam pouches.

Supply chain (25%, $212M): $100M NA micro-fulfillment (AutoStore); $70M APAC cold-chain; Blue Yonder AI (+12 pts accuracy, -$45M obsolescence).

Sustainability (20%, $170M): $90M solar/heat pumps (-25% emissions, +$12M savings); $50M wastewater 95% reuse; $30M rPET/compostables -40% virgin plastic.

Innovation/digital (10%, $85M): $40M Palo Alto fermentation/AI; $45M SAP/blockchain.

Regional: NA 40%, APAC 30%, EMEA 20%, LatAm 10%. Drives 200 bps margin expansion, fortifying 35% EBITDA.

For the full year, we are raising our guidance to 6-7% organic growth and 15%+ EBITDA margins.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Maria Gonzalez (CEO):
Good morning, John. Inflation remains a headwind, with dairy up 12%, oils 18%, and sugar 9% adding $85 million to COGS. We've mitigated through 70% hedges, targeted pricing up 3.8-4.5% with favorable elasticity at -1.8, and mix shifts to premiums. This limited gross margin pressure to 120 bps pre-offsets, and we're seeing relief as CPI cools to 2.1%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Emily Chen (JPMorgan):
What are your plans for OatFlex protein bars and what is the expected impact on volumes?

Tom Hargrove (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Emily. OatFlex is central to our HealthForward push, with 22% volume growth this quarter in the $15 billion better-for-you segment. We're launching four new flavors in Q4, targeting +250 bps ACV via club and convenience, expecting 15-20% incremental volume lift next year through high-protein snacking occasions aligned with wellness trends.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Mike Patel (Morgan Stanley):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Lisa Chen (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Mike, thanks. We've tackled Red Sea +25% freight and palm delays with SAP S/4HANA reducing inventory 8%, AI demand sensing improving forecasts 14% and stockouts 22%. New Monterrey facility and micro-fulfillment centers ensure resilience, while 45 dark stores hit 2-hour e-comm fulfillment. This unlocked $22 million working capital efficiencies.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Laura Kim with Barclays. Please proceed.

Laura Kim (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Sarah Jenkins (CFO):
Laura, we're optimistic. Q4 organic growth of 5-7% with volumes +4%, pricing +3-4%, mix +2 points. E-comm to 16-17% full-year, CapEx delivering quick paybacks. Raising FY guidance to 6-7% organic, 15%+ EBITDA margins amid category outperformance and RGM discipline.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Maria Gonzalez for closing remarks.

Maria Gonzalez (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in VitaFoods Inc. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
